scn.label: sicilianu
scn.note: Spoken in Sicily and parts of southern Calabria and Apulia; recognised as a regional language by UNESCO and Sicilian law, not by Italy as a whole.

nap.label: napulitano
nap.note: Spoken in Naples, Campania and much of southern Italy; one of the best-known Italian regional languages, with a long literary and song tradition.

vec.label: vèneto
vec.note: Spoken in Veneto, parts of Friuli, Trentino, Istria and Dalmatia, and by emigrant communities in Brazil; recognised as a regional language in Veneto.

lmo.label: lombard
lmo.note: Spoken in Lombardy, parts of Piedmont and Emilia, and in Ticino and Graubünden in Switzerland; has many local varieties.

pms.label: piemontèis
pms.note: Spoken in Piedmont in north-western Italy; recognised as a regional language by the region.

lij.label: ligure
lij.note: Spoken in Liguria, around Monaco and Mentone, and in Corsican and Sardinian enclaves; Genoese is its main variety.

ast.label: asturianu
ast.note: Spoken in Asturias in north-western Spain; protected but not official, and taught in schools.

arg.label: aragonés
arg.note: Spoken in the Pyrenean valleys of Aragon in north-eastern Spain; has few speakers and is protected but not official.

ext.label: estremeñu
ext.note: Spoken in parts of Extremadura and Cáceres province in western Spain; a small, little-standardised variety close to Leonese.

mwl.label: mirandés
mwl.note: Spoken around Miranda do Douro in north-eastern Portugal; recognised as a co-official language there since 1999.

lad.label: djudeo-espanyol
lad.note: Language of the Sephardic Jews, descended from medieval Spanish; now spoken mainly in Israel, Turkey and the Balkans, and endangered.

wln.label: walon
wln.note: Spoken in Wallonia in southern Belgium; a Romance language of the langues d'oïl, recognised as a regional language in Belgium.

pcd.label: picard
pcd.note: Spoken in Picardy and Nord-Pas-de-Calais in France and around Tournai in Belgium; a langue d'oïl.

nrf.label: normaund
nrf.note: Spoken in Normandy and the Channel Islands (Jèrriais, Guernésiais); a langue d'oïl with few speakers.

frp.label: arpetan
frp.note: Spoken in Savoy, Lyon, western Switzerland and the Aosta Valley; a Romance language distinct from both French and Occitan.

nds.label: plattdüütsch
nds.note: Spoken in northern Germany and the eastern Netherlands; recognised under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages.

bar.label: boarisch
bar.note: Spoken in Bavaria, Austria and South Tyrol; a group of Upper German dialects with many speakers.

gsw.label: alemannisch
gsw.note: Spoken in German-speaking Switzerland, Baden-Württemberg, Alsace and Vorarlberg; Swiss German is its best-known form.

ksh.label: kölsch
ksh.note: Spoken in and around Cologne in western Germany; a Ripuarian dialect protected in North Rhine-Westphalia.

stq.label: seeltersk
stq.note: Spoken by about 2,000 people in the Saterland in Lower Saxony, Germany; the last living East Frisian variety.

lim.label: limburgs
lim.note: Spoken in the Dutch and Belgian provinces of Limburg and in the neighbouring German Rhineland; recognised as a regional language in the Netherlands.

vls.label: west-vlams
vls.note: Spoken in West Flanders in Belgium, Zeelandic Flanders and French Flanders; a Dutch dialect group with a distinctive sound system.

zea.label: zeêuws
zea.note: Spoken in the province of Zeeland in the south-western Netherlands; a Dutch dialect group close to West Flemish.

sco.label: scots
sco.note: Spoken in Lowland Scotland and Ulster; a Germanic language related to English, recognised as a regional language in the UK.

cor.label: kernewek
cor.note: A Celtic language of Cornwall in south-west England; it died out as a community language in the 18th–19th century and has been revived.

glv.label: gaelg
glv.note: A Celtic language of the Isle of Man; the last native speaker died in 1974, and it has been revived and is taught in schools.

szl.label: ślōnski
szl.note: Spoken in Upper Silesia in south-western Poland and nearby Czech areas; recognised as a regional language in Poland only in debate, not by law.

rue.label: русиньскый
rue.note: Spoken by Rusyns in the Carpathians in Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine, Serbia and Croatia; recognised as a minority language in several of these countries.

ltg.label: latgalīšu
ltg.note: Spoken in Latgale in eastern Latvia; protected as a historical variety of Latvian.

sgs.label: žemaitėška
sgs.note: Spoken in Samogitia in north-western Lithuania; a Baltic variety with a separate written tradition.

vro.label: võro
vro.note: Spoken in south-eastern Estonia; a South Estonian language with its own written standard and a cultural-institution recognition.

fit.label: meänkieli
fit.note: Spoken in the Tornedalen valley in northern Sweden; recognised as an official minority language in Sweden since 2000.
